title: Troy football holds annual Fan Day as team prepares for season opener
text:
Troy football holds annual Fan Day as team prepares for season opener
Troy football players met with fans at Trojan Arena for the annual Football Fan Day on Aug. 26, following a morning practice in high temperatures. The event included autograph sessions, conversations, and opportunities for supporters to interact with the team.
Troy defensive coordinator Dontae Wright said after speaking with fans, "It reminds everybody of why you are doing it. It reminds them that all of these people are looking at them … counting on them … for some type of inspiration. It's a really good thing for these young men to be able to see that these people really care - they want to see us be successful and want to support us. They (players) know they're playing for something bigger than themselves."
Supporters like Lynda Scheid attended the event, asking players about their jersey numbers and hometowns while collecting autographs on schedule posters provided at the arena. Scheid said, "It's just that everybody is so friendly," describing her enthusiasm since she began attending Troy games in 2019.
Lines formed inside Trojan Arena as fans also met cheerleaders and T-Roy, the school mascot. Dan Heck, Deputy Athletics Director/External Relations & Revenue Generation, greeted attendees and distributed posters. Heck said, "For us, this is kind of the unofficial start of the 2026 season from a fan standpoint... This is just another reminder we're one day closer to the 2026 season." He added that such events help humanize student-athletes: "Sometimes when you're wearing a helmet or pads it's hard to put a face to the name... This is a great chance to get to know them as people."
Head coach Gerad Parker reported improvements in team depth ahead of Troy's home opener against Sam Houston on Sept. 5 at Veterans Memorial Stadium. Parker said, "We certainly feel like we have more depth... I think creating exposure in a very positive way is the whole key to this." He emphasized discipline during practices: "The definition of discipline to me is doing your job repeatedly for team glory... It's something we've spent a lot of time discussing."
Parker highlighted new wide receivers Noreel White and Howard Kinchen from junior colleges and Arkansas transfer Jace Petty as promising additions who will likely play significant roles early in the season. On defense, returning safety Justin Powe will anchor an otherwise refreshed secondary lineup.
Kicking duties remain undecided despite preseason All-American Evan Crenshaw holding down punting responsibilities; Parker described field goal and kickoff competitions as ongoing: "We've still got some steps to make... Who will kick the football off for us first—and who will take field goals first—I wouldn't be ready to give an answer yet."
